cohort: The study included 14,154 women, averaging 48.18 years in age, from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) conducted between 2007 and 2018.
finding: Urinary incontinence is linked to elevated depression odds, a relationship that appears to be moderated by dietary vitamin B12 intake.
mod_finding: A moderating role of vitamin B12 intake on depression odds in women with UI was observed among those with or without vaginal deliveries.
